How to Use This Checklist: This workbook expands the uploaded GATE 2027 Computer Science and Data Science and Artificial Intelligence preparation plan into a date-by-date checklist from 6 October 2026 to 5 February 2027.

6 October – 9 November: shared foundations including Linear Algebra, Probability and Statistics, Calculus, Discrete Mathematics, Algorithms, Programming and Data Structures, and Database Management Systems.
10 November – 7 December: Computer Science-only subjects paired with Data Science and Artificial Intelligence-only subjects.
8 December – 28 December: second pass over previous-year questions and weak-topic repair.
29 December – 11 January: revision, sectional tests and first full-length papers.
12 January – 5 February: full-length mocks, detailed analysis, weak-topic repair and final taper.
Do not tick a topic as complete after theory alone. Complete theory + topic-wise previous-year questions + second pass of errors.
Tier 1 – Must Master. Highest priority. Master completely and revise repeatedly.
Tier 2 – High Priority. Complete after Tier 1 and include in repeated practice.
Tier 3 – Important. Complete after the higher-priority topics are secure.
Tier 4 – Lower Priority. Cover if time permits. These are the first topics to move if you fall behind.
If you fall more than three days behind, do not cram. Move Tier 3 and Tier 4 topics first and preserve Tier 1 and Tier 2 topics.
Use only these categories: Conceptual, Calculation, Silly, Time Management, Guessing.
Re-solve every logged mistake after 7 days and 21 days.
For Computer Science use 2017–2026 topic-wise questions. For Data Science and Artificial Intelligence use all available papers from 2024–2026.
Spend approximately as much time analyzing a mock as taking it. Record score, accuracy, error categories, weak topics and the corrective action.
Use the final days for light review, formula sheets, marked questions, sleep and logistics rather than learning large new topics.
